title: Motifs et théorie de Hodge : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from p.39). K is a field of characteristic 0 and X is smooth projective over K. H*(X) denotes algebraic de Rham cohomology H*_dR(X/K), with its Hodge filtration F^p. On the previous page Grothendieck showed the following. If K is a locally compact non-discrete field isomorphic to C (via GAGA and Hodge theory) or to R (by Galois descent from C, since conjugation commutes with the decomposition), there is a canonical Hodge splitting phi : ⊕_{p,q} H^q(X,Ω^p) ≅ H*(X), compatible with the filtration. He then considers an abstract K together with a choice of locally compact non-discrete field topology T. In practice this means an archimedean place, i.e. an embedding K → C up to conjugation, with completion K̂_T ≅ R or C.

This page:
(1) Base change gives H*(X)_T = H*(X) ⊗_K K̂_T, and Hodge theory gives a canonical splitting phi_T : ⊕ H^q(X,Ω^p)_T → H*(X)_T.
(2) He defines H^{p,q}_T(X) = phi_T(H^q(Ω^p)_T) ∩ H*(X). This is the K-rational part of the T-adic Hodge component. It is a K-subspace of F^p H^{p+q}(X) and depends only on T.
(3) He also imposes the Betti real structure. H*(X_T, R) is the real singular cohomology of the analytic space attached to T, viewed inside H*(X)_T via the comparison isomorphism. He sets H^{p,q}_T(X,R) = phi_T(H^q(Ω^p)_T) ∩ H*(X_T,R) ∩ H*(X). This is no longer a K-space but an R_T-space, where R_T = K ∩ R ⊂ K̂_T, the 'real subfield for T'. If K̂_T ≅ R then R_T = K; if K̂_T ≅ C then R_T is the fixed field of the T-complex conjugation restricted to K.
(4) Taking all T at once, one gets a K_r-vector space, where K_r = ∩_T R_T. This is the set of elements real under every archimedean embedding, i.e. the largest totally real subfield of K. NB: since transcendental elements can be sent to non-real numbers by some embedding, K_r is algebraic over Q. This is correct: for a subfield L ⊂ K, every embedding of L extends to K, so the elements real under all embeddings form a totally real field.

Purpose. Grothendieck is setting up the comparison between three rational structures on the same space:
- the K-de Rham structure,
- the Hodge splittings at the various archimedean places,
- the real Betti structures.
He measures how much of the Hodge decomposition and of the real Betti lattice is 'rational over K'. This is a period/transcendence question. The next page ('Variations du réseau discret…, Notion de transcendance') confirms he was heading toward periods and transcendence of the Hodge decomposition.
errors: Index slip: H^{p,q}_T(X) should lie in F^p H^{p+q}(X), not F^p(H^q(X)).

The construction only makes sense for archimedean T (K̂_T ≅ R or C). If 'localement compact non discret' on p.39 is meant to include p-adic completions, there is no canonical Hodge splitting of de Rham cohomology over Q_p-type fields; only Hodge–Tate after passing to C_p with Galois action. The page tacitly restricts to K̂_T ≅ R, C.
The canonicity of phi_T when K̂_T ≅ C needs independence from the two topological automorphisms of C (identity and conjugation). This was argued on the previous page, but it is used implicitly here.
No result is stated on when these intersections are nonzero. Generically, for p ≠ q the subspace H^{p,q}_T(X) is expected to be 0 unless X has CM-type pieces, so the definitions are only a framework.

ideas.what: K-rational part of the archimedean Hodge decomposition of algebraic de Rham cohomology, H^{p,q}_T(X) = H^{p,q}(X_T) ∩ H_dR(X/K), for each archimedean place T
ideas.modern_name: Rationality of the Hodge splitting / periods; the Hodge decomposition is defined over Q̄ iff CM type (for abelian varieties)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Hodge cycles on abelian varieties 1982; Valeurs de fonctions L et périodes 1979); Shiga–Wolfart 1995, Cohen 1996 via Wüstholz analytic subgroup theorem
ideas.where_published: Related remarks on de Rham vs Betti structures appear in Grothendieck's 1966 IHES paper 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties' (footnote on periods); not this construction

ideas.what: Intersection with the real Betti structure gives a space over R_T = K ∩ R; intersecting over all archimedean T gives a vector space over the maximal totally real subfield K_r, which is algebraic over Q
ideas.modern_name: Betti/de Rham comparison with real Frobenius F_∞ (Deligne's period structures, c^±)

ideas.what: K_r = ∩_T (K ∩ R) is the largest totally real subfield and is algebraic over Q

missed.claim: Grothendieck defines, for every archimedean topology T on an arbitrary field K, the K-rational Hodge pieces and the K_r-rational 'real Hodge' pieces. He clearly intends to study how they vary with T and their link to transcendence (next page: 'Notion de transcendance'). This is a precursor of the question 'when is the Hodge decomposition defined over a number field', answered for abelian varieties (CM iff) only in the 1990s via Wüstholz's analytic subgroup theorem.
missed.quote: H^{p,q}_T(X) = φ_T(H^q(X,Ω^p_X)_T) ∩ H^*(X) ... on obtient un K_r-espace vectoriel, où K_r ≃ ∩_T R_T ≃ plus grand sous-corps tot. réel de K
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This shows Grothendieck around 1970 formulating the rationality-of-Hodge-splitting / period-transcendence problem with the comparison of all archimedean places of an arbitrary (possibly transcendental) base field. The multi-place viewpoint over a non-number-field K, reducing to the totally real algebraic subfield, is a framing not standard in the literature. Historically it is notable as an unpublished antecedent of Deligne's period formalism and of the CM characterization.

deep.surprise_reason: The definitions are natural and are subsumed by later work: Deligne's periods and absolute Hodge theory, and the transcendence results characterizing CM. Still, the explicit set-up over an arbitrary field K with all archimedean topologies at once, the reduction to the maximal totally real subfield, and the explicit link to transcendence form a modest, historically interesting unpublished detail.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'une décomposition' is likely 'on a une décomposition' or 'une décomposition canonique' (the first word is unclear).
In H^{p,q}_T(X,R) the middle term is written H^*(X_T, R) over a crossed-out symbol (possibly X_R); the transcription is acceptable.
'en fin[?], si dans tous les cas' is probably 'en faisant ∩ dans tous les cas' or 'enfin, intersectant dans tous les cas'. The sense is taking the intersection over all T.
Last line: 'NB K_r est une ext. algébrique du corps premier Q'.
